nv_black_corridor_lower_left.blurb: The left-hand half of the lower tier in the Black Corridor, a narrow sandstone slot at Red Rock in southern Nevada. Ten routes: nine bolted sport lines and a single trad line. Most sit at 5.9, with a few 5.11s, one 5.10 and one 5.12, so it suits climbers working through the moderate grades. The slot is sheltered from wind and stays in shade except around midday, and the climbing is possible in every season. That makes it popular and often busy. The walk from the car is short, well under half an hour.

nv_cave_sector_left.blurb: A sport-only wall in the Cave Sector of Hercules Gap, a limestone slot canyon crossed by a quiet paved road outside Ely in eastern Nevada. All ten routes are bolted and hard-leaning: two at 5.10, three at 5.11, three at 5.12 and two at 5.13, so there is nothing for beginners. The wall tucks into a big alcove that blocks wind and rain. It is the first sector reached when walking the road in from the east end of the gap, with the climbs on the south side.

nv_challenger_wall.blurb: A trad wall in the south fork of Pine Creek Canyon at Red Rock in southern Nevada. The sandstone is solid with good friction, and the north-facing wall stays in shade all day and can be windy, so warm layers matter for belays in cool months. Ten trad routes, nearly all at 5.11 with a single 5.10, some of them multipitch. Most now have bolted anchors, and the rest of the protection comes from a rack of cams, stoppers and small wires. A good day out for confident trad leaders.

nv_straight_shooter_wall.blurb: A short crag in Pine Creek Canyon at Red Rock in southern Nevada, on sandstone coated in dark, hard varnish over smooth rock. Seven trad lines and three sport lines mix cracks, faces and combinations. The grades split in two: a few easy 5.7s and a 5.9, then six routes around 5.11. The patina can feel slick in places and throws glare in strong light. It picks up good sun through the winter, so it works as a cold-season stop. Worth a half day if you are nearby, though not a headline wall.

nv_broast_and_toast_wall.blurb: A tall sandstone cliff in the Sandstone Quarry zone at Red Rock in southern Nevada, visible from the parking lot. Ten routes split evenly between sport and trad, mostly 5.11 with a couple each at 5.9 and 5.10 and one 5.12. Trad and mixed lines start on the lower right, while the sport routes sit up on the high left and need a scramble to reach. The wall catches sun for most of the day, and because it sees fewer climbers some lines can be sandy or crumbly until traffic cleans them up.

nv_honeycomb_boulder.blurb: A single sandstone boulder in Calico Basin at Red Rock, sitting just south of the mouth of Little Springs Canyon rather than up inside it. Ten problems, none harder than V3: four at V1, one V2 and five V3, with the easier lines among the best-rated. That spread makes it a handy stop for newer boulderers or a warm-up before harder blocs nearby. Sandstone here is fragile when damp, so choose a dry day.
